quote: Um das [-a-] analytische Krite- rium für Stabilität der Bewegung zu finden
english: To find the analytic criterion for stability of the motion.
topic: Notes on a Jacobi-type minimum criterion via regular fields of integrals, a plan to treat nonlinear (quadratic homogeneous) integral equations, and the stability of motion compared with the stability of equilibrium in hydrodynamics.

triage.modern_statement: The note is a short remark rather than a stated theorem. It seems to ask for an analytic (variational or second-variation) criterion for the stability of a steady motion of a fluid, as a counterpart to the classical Lagrange–Dirichlet energy criterion for the stability of equilibrium. Put another way: when is a steady flow, as a solution of the hydrodynamic equations, stable under perturbations? The fragment does not specify which equations (ideal or viscous fluid), which perturbations (linear or nonlinear), or which norm. Mathematically this is the general problem of hydrodynamic (and more broadly Lyapunov) stability of motion.
triage.answered_by: Not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. The general question was taken up by others; this note cannot be confirmed as Hilbert's source for any of them. Lyapunov's 1892 thesis 'The general problem of the stability of motion' gave a general analytic theory of the stability of motion. In hydrodynamics, Orr and Sommerfeld (around 1907–08) set up linear stability theory, in the hope of explaining the transition to turbulence. V. I. Arnold (1965–66) gave a variational energy criterion for the nonlinear stability of steady 2D ideal-fluid flows. It extends Rayleigh's criterion and is the closest analogue of the equilibrium energy criterion, though it covers only part of the question.

evidence.claim: Lyapunov defended his doctoral thesis 'The general problem of the stability of motion' at Moscow University on 12 October 1892.
Orr and Sommerfeld, more than a hundred years ago, conceived an approach to explain the transition from laminar to turbulent flow through hydrodynamic stability theory (the Orr–Sommerfeld equation).
Arnold proved a theorem on the nonlinear stability of steady two-dimensional flows that generalizes Rayleigh's linear stability criterion (variational principles in fluid mechanics).

Recent work gives sufficient conditions for the nonlinear stability of steady 2D ideal flows in bounded multiply-connected domains, generalizing Arnold's 1960s criterion. This shows the area is still active.
The transition to turbulence (the failure of the stability of basic flows) is described as a long-standing problem in fluid dynamics.

triage.why: The entry is a single phrase marked 'unclear' on the page. It gives no system, no class of motions and no notion of stability, so no specific problem can be identified. From the page context (stability of motion compared with stability of equilibrium in hydrodynamics), it most plausibly refers to the classical question of finding an energy- or second-variation-type criterion for steady flows. That theme was developed later by Lyapunov (general theory of the stability of motion, 1892), Orr and Sommerfeld (linear hydrodynamic stability) and Arnold (nonlinear stability of ideal flows, 1965–66). Work on the general problem, including nonlinear stability of Euler flows and the transition to turbulence, is still going on. No source links this note to those results, and no source says Hilbert himself published on it.
